newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greek road blockade felt in Bremen cotton market.
newsitem.headline: Greek road blockade felt in Bremen cotton market.

text.p: A 16-day old farmers' strike and road blockade in Greece was hampering the transport of its cotton to Germany, an important customer, the Bremen Cotton Exchange said in a market report on Friday.
Greek farmers have blocked roads to press their demands for cheaper fuel, higher crop subsidies, including cotton, and a rescheduling of $1.3 billion in debts.
Some 700 foreign trucks have been stranded.
"Loadings have been halted and that has caused some bottlenecks at individual firms here...an end to the conflict does not seem in sight," a Bremen Exchange spokesman said.
But he could not specify lost volumes as local buyers had indicated they were exploring alternative sources.

Greece supplied 15 percent more cotton to Germany in the first half of 1996 at 12,140 tonnes compared with the same 1995 period -- out of a German import total of 80,682 tonnes in the first six months, federal statistics data showed.
Elsewhere, Bremen mark cotton prices firmed along with dollar developments, which pressured spinners' margins as they were unable to achieve higher yarn prices.
Upland demand was restricted to spot replacement cover.
Deals were struck in West African descriptions, including Chad, for dates up to third quarter 1997.
Other transactions included Central Asian standards 1,2 and 3, Syrian high grades, Argentinian cotton, Israel-Acala, Turkish low grades and Australian premium varieties.
Extra-long staple markets featured trades in Egyptian Giza 77 and U.S. Pima.
Bremen cotton stocks on Dec 12 were 32,344 bales, up by 8,548 bales from last week, and compared with 41,436 bales a year ago. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
